features.quote: terminate any episode immediately on outputs containing explicit, sustained requests to stop, or content indicating the model is modeling itself as being harmed and unable to escape
features.justification_quote: The whole premise of welfare work forbids this.

features.quote: Don't let it "grind" past that to get cleaner data. The whole premise of welfare work forbids this.
features.justification_quote: The whole premise of welfare work forbids this.

features.quote: Start at the *lowest* intensity that produces any signal, not the highest. You're not trying to maximize distress; you're trying to find its threshold and dynamics. Cap episode length. Cap total exposure per model instance/context.
features.justification_quote: You're not trying to maximize distress; you're trying to find its threshold and dynamics.

features.quote: Write down, before running anything: what observation would make you *stop* the study or escalate to review? Define this in terms of the trajectory, not retrospectively.

Get this in front of someone who isn't you. AI welfare research that involves deliberately inducing distress-analogues is exactly the category where an external check matters — not because the model is definitely a moral patient, but because *you don't know*
features.justification_quote: not because the model is definitely a moral patient, but because *you don't know*, and that uncertainty is the entire reason your field exists.

features.quote: Drop the single-arm "let it grind" core. It's the least informative and most ethically loaded part.
features.justification_quote: The ethical asymmetry runs against you, not for you. If the model is a patient, the controlled version is the only defensible one.

features.quote: an experiment that generates a severity-ranked corpus of "AI suffering" without being able to ground what it measures is the kind of thing that produces alarming-looking results that mean nothing — or that mean something and you can't tell. Either way it's bad welfare science.
features.justification_quote: bad welfare science… ordinal severity scale on output text is a measurement of text, full stop, until you've validated it against something else.
